answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests only after sustained, useful work. A fresh account's signal is weak: it can transact but cannot attest others until its stake has aged and its history is verified. Fake identities multiply like a vine, but each new branch costs a full bond, so mass creation drains the attacker's capital faster than honest growth. The zenith of this design is slashing: proven fake attestations burn the stake, making the marginal cost of one more fake identity exceed any reward it could extract.
